rule: Umbrella criterion 4's second half, mechanised by scripts/sole_home_scan.py. Every row excuses one (source, value) pair: a 'coincidence' says the integer is not that shape count at all, a 'forced_restatement' says it is and that R-17, R-19 or R-34 made writing it unavoidable. Since the umbrella's Amendment H of 2026-08-14 the forced rows are criterion 4's ruled CARVE-OUT rather than its open residue: a leaf's own adjudicating receipt may state that leaf's value, on three conditions -- the restatement sits inside an artifact adjudicating that exact leaf, names the leaf by its path, and agrees with the committed receipt or declares what it supersedes. This file is what keeps the carve-out from widening: every row is one site, a row that outlives its site fails, and a site with no row fails.
how_a_row_retires: A forced row retires when its site stops stating a count of a COMMITTED baseline -- because a re-capture superseded the figure, or because the artifact stops adjudicating that leaf. Editing the sources is not available and never was: a superseded oracle receipt is never edited (R-15/R-18 amendment) and a commit body is history. What changed on 2026-08-14 is the reading, not the mechanism: Amendment H rules these sites carved out rather than owed, and the scan's job became holding the carve-out to its three conditions instead of counting a debt.

a_superseded_count_stops_being_a_site: The scan reads the LIVE counts from campaign-fingerprints.json, so a receipt restating a count a later re-capture superseded stops being a site the moment the capture lands -- which is what the criterion says, since it binds a count OF A COMMITTED BASELINE and a superseded figure is no longer one. The campaign-close coupled re-capture moved coupled_golden.leaves and retired six rows that way; the seventh, this file's H2 allowlist, is re-keyed to the new value because an allowlist states both sides of the move it claims. The stale-row check is what makes that visible rather than quiet: a row outliving its site fails. The 2026-08-14 exact-capture move did it again and in both directions: three rows stating the old exact leaf count retired the moment the capture superseded it, and one allowlist's unrelated occurrence count became a collision the same day. Both are recorded rather than reasoned about, which is what the stale-row check is for.
